"Me too, Lily. I don't like it when I sneeze. It makes my nose hurt and my eyes water. But mom says sneezing is good. It helps me get rid of the germs."

"Really? I didn't know that. Maybe sneezing is not so bad then. But I still want you to be regular again. Can I send you a card and a hug?"

"Yes, please, Lily. That would make me happy. And I will send you a card and a hug too. And when I am regular again, we can play together again. OK?"

"OK, Sam. I love you, best friend."

"I love you too, best friend. Bye, Lily."

"Bye, Sam."

But Lila did not hear him. She ran inside and slammed the door.

Sam was sad. He wanted to keep playing with Lila. He picked up her shield and knocked on the door.

"No, Sam," she said. "I don't like bees. They are scary and they sting. I don't want to play anymore."

Sam sighed. He put the shield down and walked away. He looked for another friend to play with. He wished Lila was not so distant. He missed her.

Lily said, "Tom, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to break your duck. I know you wanted to help me."

Tom said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to hurt your duck. I know you loved it."

They hugged each other. They wondered if they could fix the duck. They wondered if they could still play with it. They wondered if they could share the bathtub. They wondered if they could be friends.

Lily was so happy and played with her doll all day. From that day on, she always made sure to close the chest tight so she wouldn't lose any more toys. The end.

Jack mixed the eggs, flour, and sugar together in a bowl. Then, he added the cherries and stirred everything together. He put the cake in the oven and waited patiently. When he took it out, it smelled delicious! He put the cherries on top and shared it with his family. They loved it!

Once upon a time, there was a woman who lived in a small village. She was very slow and always took her time doing things. One day, she went to the market to buy some vegetables. While she was walking, she saw a little boy crying.

"What's wrong?" she asked.

"I lost my toy and I can't find it," the little boy replied.

"Don't worry, I can help you solve this problem," the woman said kindly.

Together, they searched for the toy and after a while, they found it. The little boy was very happy and thanked the woman. From that day on, the woman wasn't known as the slow lady anymore. She was known as the kind lady who could solve problems.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly and sing all day long. One day, Tweety saw a big, red brick on the ground. Tweety thought it looked tasty and decided to take a bite. But as soon as Tweety bit the brick, it hurt Tweety's beak. Tweety learned that bricks are not tasty and should not be bitten.

The moral of the story is that sometimes things may look good or tasty, but they can actually hurt us. It's important to be careful and think before we do something. Just like how Tweety learned not to bite bricks, we can learn from our mistakes and make better choices.

And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Tom was very excited, and watched her carefully, while she took out some parts and started fixing the car. She took out some tools, like a screw driver and hammer, and started mending the dull parts of the car. After a few minutes, Tom's mom was done and the car was working again!

Tom was delighted and thanked his mom for repairing the car. He was so happy and hugged it tight. Tom and the waffle car went for an amazing ride around the park and played many games together. Tom was so happy, he never wanted the day to end!

She went closer to the lizard and said, "Hello, lizard. Can I be your friend?" The lizard did not say anything. It just looked at Lily with its small eyes. Lily reached out her hand to pet the lizard.

But the lizard did not like that. It opened its mouth and showed its teeth. It made a hissing sound. It was scary. Lily was afraid and pulled back her hand. She ran away from the rock and cried.

"Mommy, mommy, there is a scary lizard in the garden!" she shouted.

Mommy heard Lily and came to see what was wrong. She saw the lizard on the rock. She knew it was not a bad lizard. It was just scared too.

She picked up Lily and hugged her. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. The lizard is not scary. It is just a little animal. It does not want to hurt you. It just wants to be left alone. You should not touch it or carry it. You should just look at it from far away."

Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She said, "Okay, mommy. I'm sorry, lizard. I will not bother you again. You can stay on your rock."

Mommy smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. You are a kind girl. Now, let's go and have some juice. Maybe we can find some other animals to look at in the garden. But not too close, okay?"

Lily agreed and said, "Okay, mommy. Thank you. I love you."

Mommy said, "I love you too, Lily."

They walked away from the rock and the lizard. The lizard watched them go. It was glad they were gone. It closed its mouth and relaxed its tail. It was not scary anymore. It was just a lizard.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play by the river. They had a raft that they made from wood and rope. They took turns to paddle the raft and explore the water.

One day, a new boy came to the river. His name was Carl and he had a toy boat. He saw Anna and Ben's raft and wanted to try it. He asked them, "Can you lend me your raft? I want to paddle it."

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They liked their raft and did not want to share it. But they also wanted to be nice to Carl. So they said, "OK, you can lend our raft. But be careful, it is delicate. Do not break it or lose it."

Carl thanked them and took the raft. He put his toy boat on it and paddled away. He had fun with the raft and the boat. But he did not pay attention to where he was going. He did not see the big rock in the water. He crashed the raft into the rock and it broke. The wood and rope came apart and the toy boat sank.

Carl was scared and sad. He did not know what to do. He swam back to the shore and saw Anna and Ben waiting for him. They saw the broken raft and the missing boat. They were angry and sad too. They said, "Carl, you broke our raft and lost your boat. You did not take care of our raft. You did not keep your promise. You are not a good friend."

Carl felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I am sorry, Anna and Ben. I was not careful. I was not a good friend. I should have respected your raft and your boat. Can you forgive me?"

Anna and Ben were still upset, but they also felt sorry for Carl. They said, "We forgive you, Carl. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to be more responsible and honest. You have to treat other people's things as you want them to treat yours. That is what good friends do."

Carl nodded and said, "You are right, Anna and Ben. I will try to be a better friend. Thank you for forgiving me. And thank you for lending me your raft. I am sorry I broke it. Can I help you fix it?"

Anna and Ben smiled and said, "Yes, you can help us fix it. And maybe we can play together again. But next time, be more careful and listen to us."

Carl smiled too and said, "OK, I will. Thank you, Anna and Ben. You are good friends."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of responsibility, honesty, respect, and forgiveness. It shows that lending and borrowing things requires trust and care, and that breaking or losing things can hurt other people's feelings. It also shows that apologizing and making amends can help to restore friendship and trust.

Max was sad, but he did not give up. He knew that Tom needed a friend. So, Max waited and waited. He waited until Tom was ready to play. After a long wait, Tom finally wanted to play. They played and had fun together. And from that day on, Tom was not a grumpy cat anymore.

One day, a sleepy bird named Tim wanted to fly. Tim was not like other birds. He loved to eat carrots. He had a friend, a bunny named Sam. Sam also loved carrots. They both lived in a big tree near a carrot farm.

One sunny day, Tim said to Sam, "Let's fly to the carrot farm and eat some yummy carrots!" Sam replied, "I can't fly, but I can hop very fast!" So, they went on their way to the carrot farm. They were so excited to eat their favorite food.

When they got to the farm, they ate as many carrots as they could. Tim and Sam were very happy. After eating, they went back to their big tree and took a long nap. They had a great day together, and they couldn't wait for their next adventure.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary garden, there lived a little bug. The bug had many friends, like the bee, the ant, and the butterfly. They all played together every day.

One sunny day, the bug saw the butterfly fly high in the sky. The bug wanted to learn how to fly too. So, the bug asked the butterfly, "Can you teach me to fly?"

The butterfly smiled and said, "I can try to help you learn, but you must be brave and try your best." The bug was excited and ready to learn.

They practiced every day, and the bug tried very hard. After many days, the bug finally learned how to fly. The bug was so happy and thanked the butterfly for helping. Now, the bug could fly and play with all its friends in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a bright red dress with big pockets. One day, she went for a walk in the park with her mom.

In the park, Sue saw a little bird. The bird was sad because it could not fly. Sue wanted to help the bird. She tried to pick up the bird with her hands, but it was scared. Sue had an idea. She took some bread from her pocket and gave it to the bird.

The bird ate the bread and felt better. It tried to fly again and this time, it could! The bird was so happy and flew up into the sky. Sue was proud of herself for helping the bird. She went home with her mom, smiling all the way.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a very sleepy boy. Every day, after playing with his toys, he would feel very tired. One day, Tim was playing with his toy car when he felt the urge to yawn. He knew it was time to take a nap.

Tim's mom saw him yawn and said, "Tim, you look sleepy. It's time to take a nap." Tim nodded and went to his room. He lay down on his bed and closed his eyes. As he slept, his energy started to increase.

When Tim woke up, he felt much better. He went back to playing with his toys, but this time, he played even better. His mom saw him and said, "See, Tim? Taking a nap helped you play better!"

From that day on, Tim always took naps when he felt sleepy. He learned that taking a break can help you do better at things you love. And that was the moral of the story: when you feel tired, take a rest to increase your energy and do better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was an honest boy. He always told the truth. One day, he found a key on the floor. It was shiny and pretty. He knew it was not his, but he wanted to find out what it could unlock.

Tim walked around his school, trying the key on many doors. He tried the door to the lunchroom, the door to the gym, and the door to the library. None of them would unlock. Then, he saw the door to the classroom. He put the key in the lock, turned it, and the door unlocked!

Tim felt very happy that he found what the key could unlock. He knew he should tell his teacher about the key. So, he went to his teacher and told her the honest truth. The teacher thanked Tim for being a good and honest boy. She took the key and locked the classroom door. Tim learned that being honest is always the best thing to do.

So, Tim and Sam took the bird to their home, where they took care of it. They fed it and made it feel better. The bird was very happy to have friends like Tim and Sam. Soon, the bird was all better and ready to fly again.

But soon the little duck noticed something strange. His feet began to feel heavy and he couldn't paddle anymore. He looked down and noticed he was stuck in the mud!

He started to quack in distress. Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"Don't worry, little one. I'm here to help."

The duck looked up and saw an old man with a saw. The man smiled kindly at the worried duck and said, "Let me just saw off one of your feet and then you'll be free."

The little duck was fearful, but he knew he had to trust the old man. So he nodded and watched as the man sawed off his foot and set him free.

The little duck thanked the old man and paddled away. He was thankful that the old man had been there to help him. From then on, the duck was extra careful when he went to the river, so he would not get stuck in the mud again.

"Are you okay, kids?" the park ranger asked.

"Yes, we're okay. Thank you for saving us," Lily and Tom said.

"You're welcome. But you should be more careful. This tree is old and weak. You could have fallen and hurt yourself. You should not climb too high or too fast," the park ranger said.

"We're sorry, park ranger. We were just imagining. We wanted to see more animals," Lily and Tom said.

"Imagining is good, kids. It's fun and creative. But you should also use your common sense. You should respect the nature and the rules. You should not put yourself or others in danger. Do you understand?" the park ranger said.

"Yes, we understand. We learned our lesson. We will be more careful next time," Lily and Tom said.

They hugged their moms and thanked the park ranger again. They went home and promised to be good explorers. They still imagined, but they also listened and obeyed. They realized that imagining is fun, but safety is important.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. They saw a big tree with many leaves and branches. They wanted to climb the tree and see the sky.

They ran to the tree and looked for a way to go up. Tim saw a twig on the ground. He picked it up and said, "Look, Lily, I have a magic wand. I can make anything happen with this twig."

Lily ignored him. She did not like magic. She liked real things. She said, "That is not a magic wand. That is just a twig. It cannot do anything. Let's climb the tree and find a bird's nest."

Tim was sad. He wanted Lily to play with him and his magic wand. He said, "No, Lily, this is a magic wand. Watch, I will make the tree grow bigger and bigger."

He waved the twig in the air and said, "Tree, grow bigger and bigger. Magic wand, make it happen."

Nothing happened. The tree did not grow bigger. Lily laughed. She said, "See, Tim, I told you. That is not a magic wand. That is just a twig. Come on, let's climb the tree."

She grabbed a branch and pulled herself up. Tim followed her. He did not want to be alone. He still held the twig in his hand. He hoped it was a magic wand.

They climbed higher and higher. They saw many leaves and bugs and birds. They felt the wind and the sun. They were happy.

But then, something unusual happened. The tree started to shake. The branches started to move. The leaves started to fall. The birds started to fly away.

Tim and Lily were scared. They did not know what was happening. They looked down and saw a big truck. The truck had a big saw. The saw was cutting the tree.

Tim and Lily screamed. They wanted to get down. They wanted to run away. They wanted to be safe.

Tim remembered his twig. He said, "Lily, maybe this is a magic wand. Maybe it can help us. Maybe it can stop the truck and the saw."

He waved the twig in the air and said, "Truck, stop. Saw, stop. Magic wand, make it happen."

Nothing happened. The truck did not stop. The saw did not stop. The tree kept shaking. The branches kept moving. The leaves kept falling.

Lily said, "Tim, that is not a magic wand. That is just a twig. It cannot do anything. We have to climb down and run away."

She grabbed a branch and tried to lower herself. Tim followed her. He dropped the twig. He did not want it anymore. He wanted to be safe.

They climbed down and ran away. They were scared and sad. They did not like the truck and the saw. They did not like the tree being cut.

They looked back and saw the tree falling. They heard a loud crash. They felt a big thud.

"Ahoy, matey!" Lily said. "We are the best pirates ever!"

"Arrr!" Ben said. "Look, there is another raft over there! It must be the enemy!"

They saw a small raft with a teddy bear on it. It was floating near the shore. They decided to spray it with water. They took turns to squeeze the bottle and make water come out.

"Take that, you scurvy dog!" Lily said.

"Boom, boom, boom!" Ben said.

They had so much fun spraying the water. They laughed and shouted. They did not see that the rope was getting loose. The raft was drifting away from the tree.

"Uh-oh," Lily said. "We are going too far!"

"Help!" Ben said. "We need to go back!"

They tried to paddle with their hands, but it was too hard. The water was too fast. They started to get scared.

"Mommy! Daddy!" they cried.

They hoped someone would hear them and save them. They hugged each other and prayed. They wished they had not been so adventurous.

Lily liked to record things with her new toy. It was a small box with a button and a hole. When she pressed the button, the box made a beep sound. When she spoke into the hole, the box saved her voice. Then she could press another button and hear her voice again.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a deer in the grass. It was brown and had big ears and horns. Lily wanted to record the deer. She ran towards it with her box.

"Hello, deer!" she shouted into the hole. "Can I record you?"

The deer was scared of Lily and her box. It ran away into the trees. Lily was sad. She did not understand why the deer did not want to talk to her.

Her mom and dad came to her and hugged her.

"Lily, you have to be gentle with animals," her mom said. "They are not used to loud noises and strange things. They need space and quiet to feel safe."

"But I just wanted to record the deer," Lily said. "It was so pretty and I wanted to hear its voice."

"I know, sweetie," her dad said. "But sometimes, the best way to enjoy something is to look at it and listen to it, not to touch it or record it. That way, you can respect its nature and let it be free."

Lily thought about what her mom and dad said. She realized that they were right. She felt sorry for the deer. She decided to be more careful with animals from then on.

She looked at the sky. It was gloomy and gray. It looked like it was going to rain.

"Let's go home, Lily," her mom said. "We can play with your box inside. Maybe you can record a story for us."

The police came. They went to the tent. They arrested the ringmaster. They freed the lion. They took him to a safe place. They said he deserved a better life.

Anna and Ben were happy. They were safe. They learned a lesson. They said they would never go to the circus again. They said they would rather play in the park. They said they would always stick together. They said they were the best friends in the world.

She put a stamp and a sticker on it and ran to the mail box. She hoped the hunter would find it and change his mind.

Sally giggled and said, "You're really good at this game, Benny. Let's play again!"

Later, Tim was playing with his ball. The ball rolled onto the fake ice. Tim remembered his mom's warning and did not go on the ice. He asked his mom for help. She got the ball for him and they went inside to have hot cocoa. Tim was happy he listened to his mom's warning and stayed safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big, thick tree in a small park. Many kids would play near the tree every day. One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park to play. He saw the thick tree and wanted to climb it.

As Tim tried to climb the tree, he found a small, shiny iron toy car near the tree's roots. He picked it up and said, "Wow! This car is so cool! I want to find who lost it."

Tim saw a girl named Sue playing with her toys nearby. He walked over to her and asked, "Did you lose this car?" Sue looked at the car and smiled. "Yes, I did! Thank you for finding it, Tim!"

From that day, Tim and Sue became best friends. They would meet at the park every day and play with their toys under the thick tree. They shared many fun times together and always took care of each other.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a small mushroom. This mushroom was not like the others. It was dangerous. It could make you very sick. The other mushrooms were not dangerous.

One day, a little bunny saw the dangerous mushroom. The bunny said, "I want to eat you." The mushroom answered, "No, don't eat me! I am dangerous. I can make you sick." The bunny did not listen. He wanted to eat the mushroom.

The bunny ate the dangerous mushroom. He got very sick. His friend, a wise old owl, saw him. The owl said, "You should have listened to the mushroom. Now you are sick." The bunny learned his lesson. He knew he should always listen to others.

The moral of the story is to always listen to what others have to say.

Suddenly, Benny heard a voice behind him. "Stop right there, little bunny!" It was the garden owner, Mr. Johnson. "You can't play with my velvet pillow. It's for decoration only," he said.

Benny felt sad and wanted to go back to his burrow. But then he remembered that he was an independent bunny and he could solve this problem on his own. He hopped over to Mr. Johnson and said, "I'm sorry, Mr. Johnson. I didn't know the velvet pillow was special. Can I help you with anything else in the garden?"

Mr. Johnson smiled and said, "Thank you for apologizing, Benny. Yes, you can help me pick some carrots for dinner." Benny was happy to help and they worked together until the sun went down. From that day on, Benny knew that being independent meant being responsible and respectful.

As the days went by, they noticed something was wrong. They felt distant from each other. They didn't laugh as much as before. Mommy and Daddy talked and talked until they realized they needed to work on their marriage. They hugged and kissed and promised to love each other forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hear stories from her mommy every night before bed. One day, Lily found a shiny rock while playing outside. She brought it inside to show her mommy.

Mommy took the rock and examined it closely. She said it was very pretty and that Lily should keep it safe. Lily was so happy and excited to have her very own treasure.

But when Lily's friends came over to play, she showed them the rock and they said it wasn't special at all. Lily felt ashamed and sad. She didn't want to show her treasure to anyone anymore.

Mommy noticed that Lily was upset and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her the story and mommy hugged her tight. She said that Lily's rock was special because it was hers and that's all that mattered. From then on, Lily wasn't ashamed anymore and she kept her treasure close to her heart.

Lily was sad and started to cry. "I want that toy, mommy!" she said. "I'm sorry, sweetie, but we can't buy it," her mommy replied. Lily refused to leave the store without the toy. "I don't want any other toy, mommy. I want that one!" she said, still crying.

"Can we have a lollipop, mom?" Ben and Sam asked.

"Sure, but only one each, and after lunch," their moms said.

Ben and Sam waited for lunch. They were hungry and excited. They ate their sandwiches and fruits quickly. Then they ran to the truck. They saw a man give lollipops to other kids. They waited for their turn.

"Here you go, boys. One lollipop each. Enjoy!" the man said.

"Thank you!" Ben and Sam said. They took their lollipops and smiled. Ben had a red one and Sam had a blue one.

They licked their lollipops and walked back to their moms. They were happy. But then, something bad happened. Sam was clumsy. He tripped on a rock and fell down. His lollipop flew out of his hand and landed on the ground. It broke into pieces.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Sam cried. He hurt his knee and his hand. He also lost his lollipop.

Ben saw what happened. He felt sorry for Sam. He wanted to help him. He had an idea. He ran to Sam and gave him his lollipop.

"Here, Sam. You can have my lollipop. I don't need it. You are my friend," Ben said.

Sam looked at Ben. He saw his red lollipop. He smiled. He took his lollipop and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. You are my friend, too."

They hugged each other. They were happy again. They licked their lollipops and walked back to their moms. Their moms saw what happened. They were proud of Ben. They gave him a hug and a kiss.

"Ben, you did a very good thing. You shared your lollipop with Sam. You are a good friend. We love you," they said.

Ben felt warm and happy. He learned a lesson. He learned that sharing is caring. He learned that being a good friend is better than having a lollipop. He learned that he was lucky to have Sam. He learned that he was happy.

"Hey, Ben, do you want to play a game with me?" Sara asks.

"What game?" Ben says.

"It's a guessing game. I will put something in my mouth and you have to guess what it is. If you guess right, you get a point. If you guess wrong, I get a point. The one with the most points wins. Do you want to play?" Sara explains.

"OK, I want to play. You go first," Ben agrees.

Sara looks around and sees a red crayon on the table. She picks it up and puts it in her mouth. She makes a funny face and says, "Mmm, mmm."

Ben looks at her and thinks. He knows that Sara likes to draw with crayons, but he also knows that crayons are not good to eat. He decides to guess.

"Is it a crayon?" Ben asks.

Sara takes the crayon out of her mouth and spits. She nods and says, "Yes, it is a crayon. You are right. You get a point. But don't tell Mommy. She will be mad."

Ben smiles and says, "OK, I won't tell. Now it's my turn. Close your eyes."

Sara closes her eyes and waits. She hears Ben open the fridge and take something out. She wonders what it is. She hopes it is something yummy.

"OK, you can open your eyes now," Ben says.

"Is it a grape?" Sara guesses.

Ben shakes his head and says, "No, it is not a grape. It is a lime. You are wrong. I get a point. But don't tell Daddy. He will be sad."

Sara makes a sour face and says, "OK, I won't tell. But limes are not good to eat. They are too sour."

Ben takes the lime out of his mouth and says, "I know. But they are fun to make faces with. Do you want to try?"

Sara nods and says, "OK, I want to try. But let's play another game after. This game is too hard."

Ben agrees and says, "OK, let's play another game. But first, let's have some water. Our mouths are dry."

Just then, a sweet little bird flew down, saying, "I can clean it, Croaky! I'm mighty strong and I know how to organize things."

Croaky was so astonished, he thanked the bird and watched as she began to organize all the produce in the store. After a few minutes, the grocery store was shiny and clean. Croaky smiled and said, "Thanks for cleaning the store!" The little bird flew away, chirping proudly.

Once upon a time there was a young man who was feeling gloomy because he had lost his job. He decided to go and gather the courage to try his luck at the university nearby. He was sure that the university would be a great place to find something new.

He gathered his backpack, put on his hat and set off for his destination. Along the way he met an old man whom he asked about the university. The old man said "Ah, you are going to the university, are you? I have a word of warning; do not go there."

But the young man was determined and ignored the old man's warning. He arrived at the university and found a sign which said "Job Openings". The young man was elated and gathered his courage to wait in the queue that formed for the job openings. He was sure he would get the job. 

However, some hours later the young man was left standing alone outside the university. His heart filled with despair as he realized that no one had chosen him for the job. Without a job, he had no money and nowhere he could go. 

The young man gathered his bag, feeling gloomier than ever, and he walked back home. He had learned a valuable lesson; sometimes, we should listen to the advice others give us. If only he had listened to the old man's warning!

Once upon a time, there were two friends; a sheep and a rabbit. The sheep had lots and lots of wool, which it was very proud of! 

One day, the rabbit said to the sheep, "I think your wool is a bit messy, can I help you catch it and clean it up?".

The sheep was a bit wary of the idea, but eventually agreed. So the rabbit helped catch the loose pieces of wool and make them neat without being too rough. 

The rabbit was very good at it, but then the sheep asked, "How do I keep it like this?".

The rabbit thought long and hard and had a great idea. "Let me make a wool scarf for you! That way we can tie up your wool and it won't get messy again".

So the rabbit made a beautiful wool scarf for the sheep. The sheep was so happy with it, than thanked the rabbit for all its help. 

From that day on, the sheep always kept its wool scarf on to keep it neat and tidy, and the two friends were very happy together.

Lila and Tom are friends who like to play outside. One day, they find a map in a book. The map shows a big X in the east. Lila and Tom want to find the X. They think it is a treasure.

They take the map and a backpack. They put some snacks and a bottle of water in the backpack. They are very organized. They say goodbye to their moms and start to walk. They follow the map and look for signs.

They see a big tree, a red barn, a yellow bridge and a blue lake. They are on the right path. They are happy and excited. They talk to each other.

"Maybe the treasure is gold or jewels," Lila says.

"Or maybe it is candy or toys," Tom says.

They walk and walk until they see a hill. The map says the X is on the hill. They climb the hill and search for the X. They look under rocks and bushes. They look behind trees and flowers. They look everywhere.

But they cannot find the X. They are sad and tired. They sit on the grass and eat some snacks. They drink some water. They look at the map again.

"Maybe the map is wrong," Lila says.

"Or maybe someone took the treasure," Tom says.

They are about to give up when they hear a voice.

"Hello, children. What are you doing here?"

They look up and see a man. He is wearing a hat and a coat. He has a big smile and a big beard. He is holding a shovel and a bag.

"We are looking for the treasure," Lila says.

"What treasure?" the man asks.

"The treasure on the map," Tom says. He shows the man the map.

The man laughs. He says, "Oh, this is not a treasure map. This is a gardening map. I made it to show where I planted some seeds. The X is where I planted some carrots. They are not ready yet. Do you want to see?"

Lila and Tom are surprised. They say, "Yes, please."

The man takes them to the X. He digs a hole and pulls out a carrot. He gives it to Lila. He digs another hole and pulls out another carrot. He gives it to Tom.

"Here you go. These are your treasures. Fresh and healthy. Enjoy," he says.

Lila and Tom thank the man. They wash the carrots and bite them. They are crunchy and sweet. They are happy and satisfied.

They say goodbye to the man and start to walk back. They still have the map and the backpack. They are very organized. They follow the map and look for signs.

They see the blue lake, the yellow bridge, the red barn and the big tree. They are on the right path. They are happy and excited. They talk to each other.

"Maybe the treasure is not gold or jewels," Lila says.

"Or candy or toys," Tom says.

"Maybe the treasure is something else," they say together.

They smile and hug. They are friends who like to play outside. They have found their treasure.

"Oh no, Rex!" Tom says. "You are so muddy! We have to go home and wash you!"

"Stop it, Rex!" Tom says. "You have to wash or you will smell bad!"

Rex does not listen. He jumps out of the bathtub and runs around the house. He leaves wet paw prints on the floor and the couch and the bed. Tom chases him and tries to catch him.

"Come back, Rex!" Tom says. "You are making a mess!"

Rex runs into the kitchen and sees a cake on the table. He thinks the cake looks yummy. He jumps on the table and eats the cake. Tom sees him and gets very angry.

"Rex!" Tom says. "That was my cake! Bad dog!"

Rex feels sorry. He wags his tail and licks Tom's face. Tom sighs and hugs Rex.

"I love you, Rex," Tom says. "But you are still a hairy, muddy, cake-eating dog. And you need a wash!"

The cat decided to try it out. So it got a brush and began to paint. After a few minutes, the cat had created a stunning masterpiece. Everyone was so impressed by the cat's painting. 

The cat was so happy. It knew that it would make the most beautiful print that the world had ever seen. And so they did. The cat and its prints have been admired by everyone ever since.

Once upon a time, there was a bad boy who did not do what he was told. He was always rude and never listened. His mum was really mad!

One day, she said, "I think it's time to punish you". He was so scared!

His mum got out a big weight from the cupboard. It was very thin and light. She said, "I want you to hold this weight for one whole hour without dropping it. If you do, you will be punished more".

The boy was so scared. He tried hard to hold the weight for the whole hour, but his little arms got really tired. He dropped it after just 35 minutes.

"Oh no!" His mum said very angrily. She said, "That was not good enough. Now you must do something else to be punished".

The bad boy had learned his lesson - he must always do what he is told!

Each time he felt better and each time he became less ashamed. Soon he was happily praying out loud at the fountain and all the birds sang along with him. He had found a place to be happy and he was no longer scared or ashamed.

Mark's dad said it was a big fish and quickly reeled it in. Mark watched excitedly as the big fish on top of the surface of the water. What a big and thick fish it was! They both cheered as they marked the fish from the line and put it in the bucket.

One day, Sara saw a poster for a big opera show. She wanted to go and see the real opera singers. She asked her mom and dad to take her, but they said no. They said the show was too long and too late and too expensive. They said Sara was too young and too noisy and too rude. They said she had to stay home and be quiet.

Sara was very mad. She decided to go to the opera show by herself. She took some money from her mom's purse and sneaked out of the house. She walked and walked until she found the big theater. She bought a ticket and went inside. She was very excited.

The theater was very dark and very fancy. There were many people in nice clothes and shiny jewels. They looked at Sara with surprise and scorn. They did not like her dirty dress and messy hair. They did not like her loud voice and silly questions. They did not include her in their talk or smiles.

The opera show started. Sara did not understand the words or the music. She did not like the costumes or the scenery. She did not like the opera singers. She thought they were boring and ugly and old. She wanted to sing instead of them. She wanted to show them how good she was.

She waited for a quiet moment. Then she jumped on the stage and started to sing. She sang very loud and very bad. She sang with her nose and her tongue and her teeth. She sang with her arms and her legs and her feet. She sang with her eyes and her ears and her hair. She sang with everything she had.

The people in the theater were shocked and angry. They booed and hissed and threw things at Sara. They told her to stop and go away and never come back. They called her a brat and a pest and a fool. They did not like her singing. They did not like her at all.

Sara was scared and hurt. She ran off the stage and out of the theater. She cried and cried and cried. She wished she had listened to her mom and dad. She wished she had stayed home and been quiet. She wished she had been nicer and politer and kinder.

She walked and walked until she found her house. She hoped her mom and dad would forgive her and hug her and love her. But when she got to the door, she saw a big sign. It said: "We have gone to the opera. Do not wait for us. We do not want you anymore. You are an empty child."

The end.

Moral: Do not be selfish and rude. Respect other people and their feelings. Learn to appreciate and enjoy different things. Or you will end up alone and unhappy.

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play by the sea. They liked to look for shells and rocks and crabs. One day, they saw a big pile of oysters on the sand. They ran to the pile and started to pick up the oysters.

"Look, Tim, this one is so shiny!" Sam said, holding an oyster with a pearl inside.

"Wow, Sam, you are so lucky!" Tim said, feeling jealous. He wanted a pearl too. He looked at his oysters, but they were all plain and gray.

"Can I have your pearl, Sam?" Tim asked, trying to sound nice.

"No, Tim, this is my pearl. I found it first. It is fair," Sam said, holding the oyster close to his chest.

Tim was angry. He wanted the pearl more than anything. He thought of a plan. He waited until Sam was not looking, and then he grabbed the oyster with the pearl and ran away.

"Hey, Tim, give me back my oyster!" Sam shouted, chasing after him.

But Tim was faster. He ran to the rocks and hid behind them. He opened the oyster and took out the pearl. He smiled and put the pearl in his pocket.

But then, he felt a sharp pain in his hand. He looked and saw that the oyster had cut him. He saw blood dripping from his hand. He cried out in pain and fear.

Sam heard him and ran to the rocks. He saw Tim holding his hand and crying. He saw the oyster and the pearl on the ground.

"Tim, what did you do?" Sam asked, feeling sorry for him.

"I'm sorry, Sam, I'm sorry. I wanted your pearl. I was bad. Please help me," Tim said, sobbing.

Sam felt sad and angry. He picked up his oyster and his pearl. He looked at Tim and shook his head.

"No, Tim, I can't help you. You were not fair. You were not a good friend. You hurt yourself and you hurt me. You have to go to the doctor and tell the truth. Goodbye, Tim," Sam said, walking away.

Tim was left alone, with his hand bleeding and his heart broken. He wished he had never seen the pearl. He wished he had been fair and a good friend. He learned a hard lesson that day. He lost his pearl and his friend. He was very sorry.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they disagree. One day, Mom says they have to go to the grocery with her. Lily and Max do not want to go. They think the grocery is boring.

"Can we stay home and play?" Lily asks.

"No, you have to come with me. It will be quick," Mom says.

Lily and Max sigh. They put on their shoes and coats. They follow Mom to the car. They sit in the back seat and make faces at each other.

At the grocery, Mom gives them each a basket. She tells them to help her find some things. Lily and Max disagree on what to get. Lily wants to get apples, but Max wants to get bananas. Lily wants to get cheese, but Max wants to get yogurt. Lily wants to get bread, but Max wants to get crackers.

"Stop disagreeing!" Mom says. "We need all these things. You can share them later."

Lily and Max are not happy. They keep arguing. They do not notice that they are making a lot of noise. They do not notice that they are bumping into other people. They do not notice that they are dropping things from their baskets.

Suddenly, they hear a loud crash. They turn around and see that they have knocked over a pile of cans. The cans are rolling everywhere. The people are looking at them. Mom is looking at them. Lily and Max feel very bad.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Lily says.

"I'm sorry, too," Max says.

Mom helps them pick up the cans. She pays for the things. She takes them back to the car. She is not angry, but she is not happy either.

"Lily and Max, you need to learn to get along," she says. "Disagreeing is okay, but you have to be respectful and polite. You have to listen to each other and to me. You have to be careful and helpful. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nod. They hug Mom and say they love her. They hug each other and say they are sorry. They decide to share the apples, the bananas, the cheese, the yogurt, the bread, and the crackers. They realize that going to the grocery is not so boring after all. They learn that disagreeing can be good, but only if they do it nicely.

Sam loves to drive his toy car. He has a big wheel that he can turn to make the car go left or right. He likes to pretend that he is a race car driver and zoom around the house.

One day, he sees his friend Max playing with a new toy car. Max's car has lights and sounds and can go very fast. Sam wants to play with Max's car, but Max says no. He says that his car is better than Sam's car and that Sam's car is old and boring.

Sam feels sad and angry. He thinks that Max is not a loyal friend. He goes to his room and hugs his toy car. He tells his car that he still loves it and that it is the best car in the world. He says that he will never trade it for anything.

His mom hears him talking to his car and comes to his room. She asks him what is wrong. Sam tells her what Max said and how he hurt his feelings. His mom hugs him and says that she is sorry that Max was mean to him. She says that Sam's car is very special and that it was a gift from his dad. She says that Sam's car is not old and boring, but classic and fun.

She also says that Sam is a very loyal and kind boy and that he deserves loyal and kind friends. She says that maybe Max is just jealous of Sam's car and that he does not know how to share. She says that Sam can try to talk to Max and explain how he feels, or he can find other friends who will appreciate his car and his personality.

Sam feels better after talking to his mom. He decides to give Max another chance and see if he can be a loyal friend. He also decides to invite some other friends over to play with his car and have a race. He thinks that driving his car is more fun when he has good friends to share it with. He smiles and thanks his mom for her advice. He says that he loves her and his car very much.

Ben and Lily were playing in their room. They liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things. They had a big closet with many clothes and toys inside. Sometimes they would lift the clothes and look for hidden treasures.

One day, they saw something shiny under a pile of sweaters. They lifted the sweaters and found a small box. It was silver and had a lock on it. They wondered what was inside.

"Maybe it's a treasure!" Ben said.

"Maybe it's a secret!" Lily said.

They tried to open the box, but it was too hard. They needed a key. They looked around the room, but they could not find one.

"Where is the key?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it's in the closet too." Lily said.

They decided to search the closet for the key. They lifted more clothes and toys, but they did not find the key. They found other things, like a hat, a ball, a book, and a doll. They put them on the floor and kept looking.

As they lifted more things, they saw a dark corner in the back of the closet. It was unknown to them. They had never looked there before. They felt curious and scared.

"What's there?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Let's see." Lily said.

They moved closer to the dark corner. They lifted a blanket and saw a small hole. It was big enough for them to crawl through. They wondered what was on the other side.

"Maybe it's a new place!" Ben said.

"Maybe it's a surprise!" Lily said.

They decided to go through the hole. They held hands and crawled into the unknown. They hoped to find the key and the treasure. They did not know what they would see.

Tom and Sam were new at school. They had to unpack their bags and put on their uniforms. Tom did not like his uniform. It was too big and itchy. He felt uncomfortable.

"Can I take it off?" he asked his teacher.

"No, you have to wear it. It is the rule," the teacher said.

Tom was sad. He wanted to wear his own clothes. He looked at Sam. Sam had a nice uniform. It fit him well and it was soft. Sam smiled at Tom.

"Hi, I'm Sam. Do you want to be friends?" he asked.

Tom nodded. He liked Sam. He hoped they could play together.

They went to the playground. There were many other kids. Some of them were nice. Some of them were mean. The mean kids saw Tom and Sam. They laughed at them.

"Look at them! They are so funny!" one of them said.

"Yeah, especially Tom. His uniform is so ugly and big. He looks like a clown!" another one said.

They ran to Tom and Sam. They pushed them and pulled their uniforms. They made fun of them.

"Stop it! Leave us alone!" Tom and Sam cried.

But the mean kids did not stop. They kept hurting them. Tom and Sam felt scared and hurt. They wished they could go home.

The teacher saw what was happening. She ran to the playground. She shouted at the mean kids.

"Stop it right now! How dare you bully them? Go to the office. You are in big trouble!" she said.

The mean kids ran away. They were afraid of the teacher. The teacher helped Tom and Sam. She checked their uniforms and their bodies. They had tears and bruises.

"I'm so sorry. Are you okay?" she asked.

Tom and Sam shook their heads. They were not okay. They felt bad.

"Can we go home?" they asked.

The teacher sighed. She felt sorry for them. She wished she could let them go home. But she could not.

"No, you have to stay. It is the rule," she said.

Tom and Sam were sad. They had to stay at school. They had to wear their uniforms. They had to face the mean kids. They did not like school. They wanted to go home. They wanted to wear their own clothes. They wanted to be happy.

Lily and Ben love to play outside. They like to run, jump, and climb. One day, they see a huge fly on a flower. The fly is black and shiny, with big eyes and wings.

"Wow, look at that fly!" Ben says. "It is so big and fast!"

"Can we catch it?" Lily asks. "I want to see it up close."

They try to catch the fly, but it is too smart. It flies away when they get near. It goes to another flower, then another, then another.

"Stop, fly, stop!" Ben shouts. "We just want to play with you!"

The fly does not stop. It does not want to play. It wants to drink nectar from the flowers. It does not like Lily and Ben.

"Maybe we can make it like us," Lily says. "Maybe we can give it something."

"Like what?" Ben asks.

"Like a snack," Lily says. "Flies like snacks, right?"

She looks around and sees a cookie on the ground. Someone dropped it and left it there. It is dirty and has ants on it.

"Here, fly, here!" Lily says. She picks up the cookie and holds it out. "We have a snack for you! It is yummy and sweet!"

The fly sees the cookie and smells it. It likes the smell. It flies towards the cookie. It lands on it and starts to eat.

"Yay, we got it!" Ben says. He runs to Lily and the cookie. "Now we can see it and touch it!"

But the fly does not like to be touched. It feels Ben's hand and gets scared. It flies away again, very fast.

"Hey, come back, fly!" Ben says. "We are not going to hurt you!"

But the fly does not come back. It flies far away, where Lily and Ben cannot see it.

Lily and Ben are sad. They wanted to play with the fly, but the fly did not want to play with them.

"Maybe we should find another friend," Lily says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But who?"

They look around and see a butterfly. The butterfly is colorful and pretty, with orange and black wings.

"Wow, look at that butterfly!" Lily says. "It is so beautiful and graceful!"

"Can we catch it?" Ben asks. "I want to see it up close."

They try to catch the butterfly, but it is too fast. It flies away when they get near. It goes to another flower, then another, then another.

"Stop, butterfly, stop!" Lily shouts. "We just want to play with you!"

The butterfly does not stop. It does not want to play. It wants to drink nectar from the flowers. It does not like Lily and Ben.

"Maybe we can make it like us," Ben says. "Maybe we can give it something."

"Like what?" Lily asks.

"Like a flower," Ben says. "Butterflies like flowers, right?"

He looks around and sees a flower on a bush. It is pink and pretty, with a nice smell.

"Here, butterfly, here!" Ben says. He picks the flower and holds it out. "We have a flower for you! It is pretty and nice!"

The butterfly sees the flower and smells it. It likes the smell. It flies towards the flower. It lands on it and starts to drink.

"Yay, we got it!" Lily says. She runs to Ben and the flower. "Now we can see it and touch it!"

But the butterfly does not mind to be touched. It feels Lily's hand and does not get scared. It stays on the flower and on Lily's hand.

"Hey, look, butterfly!" Ben says. "We are not going to hurt you!"

The butterfly does not fly away. It stays with Lily and Ben. It likes them.

Lily and Ben are happy. They found a friend who likes them. They play with the butterfly and the flower.

"Can we keep it?" Lily asks.

"Sure," Ben says. "But we have to be gentle and kind."

They are gentle and kind. They include the butterfly in their games. They run, jump, and climb with the butterfly. They have fun.

The end.

Tim and Kim are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They are happy.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He is mean. He pushes Tim and Kim. He says, "This is my park. Go away. You are weak and silly." He laughs.

Tim and Kim are sad and scared. They want to go home. But then, they have an idea. They say, "We are not weak and silly. We are tough and smart. We have a name. We are Tim and Kim. And we are friends. We can share the park. You can play with us. But you have to be nice."

The big boy is surprised. He does not know what to say. He feels bad. He says, "I am sorry. I was mean. I have a name too. I am Ben. Can I play with you?"

Tim and Kim smile. They say, "Yes, you can play with us. But you have to be nice. And you have to say sorry to everyone you pushed."

Ben nods. He says sorry to everyone. He feels better. He plays with Tim and Kim. They swing, slide and run. They are happy.

At the end of the day, Tim and Kim give Ben a kiss on the cheek. They say, "You are our friend now. We like you. See you tomorrow."

Ben smiles. He says, "Thank you. You are my friends too. I like you. See you tomorrow."

The moral of the story is: Be nice to others. Share and play. Make friends. Kiss and hug.

Her mom said, "That's right. Now, watch my fingers and follow me. We will play the song together."

Lily watched her mom's fingers and tried to copy them. She pressed the keys on the piano and made sounds. She heard the song in her ears. She liked the song. She played it with her mom. They played it again and again.

Lily was very happy. She learned the new song. She thanked her mom and gave her a hug. Her mom said, "You are very smart, Lily. You learned the song very fast. I am proud of you."

But the magnet was too strong. It snapped to everything metal. It snapped to the lamp, to the scissors, to the coins. It was hard to pull it off.

Sam and Mia thought it was fun. They tried to snap the magnet to each other. They laughed when it snapped to their buttons, their zippers, their hair clips. They snapped it to their ears, their noses, their fingers. It tickled and pinched.

But then, Sam had a bad idea. He saw a small metal thing on the floor. It was shiny and pointy. It was a needle. Sam did not know what it was. He thought it was a toy. He picked it up and tried to snap it to the magnet.

But the needle was dangerous. It was sharp and hurtful. It poked Sam's hand and made it bleed. Sam cried out in pain. He dropped the needle and the magnet. Mia saw what happened and ran to help him. She wrapped his hand in a cloth and hugged him. She told him to be careful. She said the needle was not a toy. She said the magnet was too strong. She said they should not play with them anymore.

One day, a little girl named Anna wanted to write a letter to Santa. She asked her mom for some paper and a crayon. She wrote her name and drew a picture of a reindeer. She wanted a reindeer toy for Christmas.

She showed her letter to her mom and said, "Mom, can you help me send this to Santa? I want a reindeer like this one."

Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, honey. We can put it in the mailbox. But you know, Santa is very busy. He has many letters to read and many toys to make. He might not have a reindeer toy for you. What else do you want for Christmas?"

Anna thought for a moment and said, "I want a book. And a doll. And a puzzle. And a ball. And a bike. And a..."

Her mom interrupted her and said, "Wow, that's a lot of things. Do you really need all of them? What about the other children who have nothing? Don't you think Santa should share his toys with them too?"

Anna looked at her mom and said, "But I want them all. They are fun and pretty and cool."

Her mom said, "I know, honey. But sometimes, less is more. You can have more fun with one toy that you love than with many toys that you don't care about. And you can make someone else happy by giving them a toy that you don't need. That's what Christmas is about. Sharing and caring."

Anna thought about what her mom said. She looked at her letter and said, "Mom, can I change my letter? I don't want a reindeer toy anymore. I want to give it to someone who needs it more. Can I write that to Santa?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "Of course, honey. That's very kind and generous of you. I'm sure Santa will be very proud of you. And maybe he will have a surprise for you too."

Anna took her crayon and wrote on her letter, "Dear Santa, please give my reindeer toy to someone who needs it more. I have enough toys. Thank you. Love, Anna."

She put her letter in the mailbox and felt happy. She hoped that her reindeer toy would make another child smile. She was alert and listened for Santa's sleigh. She wondered what surprise he would bring her.

The end.

One day, her grandma said, "Anna, you can help me pick some beans. They are ready to eat. But be careful, there are some bugs that like to eat them too."

Anna nodded and followed her grandma to the garden. She saw some shiny green beans hanging from the plants. She reached out to grab one, but then she saw a big black bug with red spots on it. It was sitting on the bean and looked angry.

Anna was scared of the bug. She screamed and let go of the bean. She ran back to her grandma and hugged her leg.

"Grandma, there is a big bug on the bean! It is scary and ugly!"

Her grandma smiled and said, "Don't be scared, Anna. That is a ladybug. It is not a bad bug. It is a good bug. It helps the garden by eating the small bugs that hurt the plants. It is not angry, it is just doing its job. It won't hurt you or the bean. You can admire it, but don't touch it."

Anna looked at the ladybug again. She saw that it was not so big or scary. It was actually kind of pretty, with its red spots and shiny wings. She felt sorry for screaming at it.

She said, "I'm sorry, ladybug. I didn't know you were a good bug. You can have the bean. I will pick another one."

She found another bean that was free of bugs and picked it. She showed it to her grandma and said, "Look, grandma, I picked a bean for dinner. Can I pick more?"

Her grandma nodded and said, "Yes, you can, Anna. You are a good helper. And you are brave, too. You learned something new today. You learned to admire the ladybug and the vegetable garden."

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big slide and run to it.

"Me first!" Tim says. He climbs up the ladder and slides down. He has a big smile on his face.

"Me next!" Sam says. He follows Tim and slides down. He also has a big smile on his face.

They take turns sliding and smiling. They have fun.

But then, they see an old man sitting on a bench. He has a cane and a hat. He does not have a smile on his face. He looks sad.

"Who is he?" Tim asks.

"I don't know," Sam says.

"Let's go say hi," Tim says.

They walk to the bench and stand in front of the old man.

"Hi, mister," Tim says.

"Hello, boys," the old man says.

"What are you doing here?" Sam asks.

"I'm just resting," the old man says.

"Don't you want to play?" Tim asks.

"I'm too old to play," the old man says.

"That's not true," Sam says. "You can play with us."

"Yeah, come on," Tim says. "We have cars and balls."

They take their toys and show them to the old man. He looks at them and smiles a little.

"Thank you, boys," he says. "But I can't play with you. I have a bad leg and a bad back. I can't run or slide or throw."

"That's okay," Tim says. "You can watch us play. And we can talk to you. And we can make you smile."

The old man nods and smiles more. He likes the boys. They are kind and friendly.

They sit on the bench and talk to the old man. They tell him their names and their favorite colors and their favorite animals. They ask him his name and his favorite things. They make jokes and laugh.

The old man feels happy. He forgets his pain and his loneliness. He enjoys the boys' company.

They play and talk and smile. They have fun.

Their moms see them and smile too. They are proud of their boys. They are good boys.

The moral of the story is: You can make friends with anyone, no matter how old or different they are. You can share your toys and your time and your smile. You can make someone's day better. You can be kind and friendly.

"Hey, stop!" Tom shouts. "This is our house!"

But Spot does not listen. He is too excited. He jumps on the box. He makes the box shake. He makes the box fall. He traps Tom and Ann inside.

"Help!" Tom and Ann cry. "We are stuck!"

Spot barks. He thinks they are playing. He wags his tail. He licks the box.

Tom and Ann are not happy. They are scared. They want to get out. They push the box. They kick the box. They make a lot of noise.

Their mom hears them. She comes to the living room. She sees the box. She sees Spot. She understands what happened.

She lifts the box. She frees Tom and Ann. She hugs them. She says, "Are you okay?"

Tom and Ann nod. They are okay. They are glad to see their mom. They are not mad at Spot. They know he did not mean to trap them.

They say, "We are sorry, mom. We made a mess."

Their mom smiles. She says, "It's okay. I like your house. It is very creative. But maybe next time, you can play with Spot too. He wants to be your friend."

Tom and Ann agree. They say, "Okay, mom. We will play with Spot too."

They pet Spot. They say, "Sorry, Spot. We love you."

Spot wags his tail. He says, "Woof!"

They all laugh. They are happy. They do not mind the rain. They have each other.

One day, a fisherman went to the lake with his boat. He wanted to catch some fish for his family. He had a rod, a hook and a worm. He threw the hook into the water and waited.

Soon, he felt a tug on his rod. He pulled hard and saw a big fish on his hook. He was very happy. He put the fish in his basket and threw the hook again.

But then, he heard a splash. He looked and saw a little boy in the water. The boy was scared and cold. He had fallen from the shore. The fisherman quickly rowed his boat to the boy and helped him out.

"Are you okay?" the fisherman asked.

"Yes, thank you," the boy said. "You saved me. I was playing with my ball and it rolled into the water. I tried to get it but I slipped and fell."

"Where is your ball?" the fisherman asked.

"It is over there," the boy said, pointing to a red ball floating near the shore.

The fisherman rowed his boat to the ball and gave it to the boy. The boy hugged his ball and smiled.

"Thank you again," the boy said. "You are very kind."

The fisherman smiled too. He was glad he could help the boy. He said goodbye and rowed his boat back to the lake. He thought catching fish was easy, but saving a boy was more important.

"Look, a firefly!" Ben said.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said.

The firefly flew closer to them. It saw their tears. It felt sorry for them. It wanted to help them.

"Hello, little ones. Why are you crying?" the firefly said.

"We are lost. We can't find our way out of the hole," Ben said.

"Don't worry. I can show you the way. Follow me," the firefly said.

"Thank you, firefly. You are very kind," Lily said.

"Spicy? Like what?" Ben asked.

"Wow, that sounds scary. We won't go in the hole again. We promise," Ben said.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be fair and to think of others when playing games. Everyone deserves a chance to play, and winning isn't everything.

One day, a little fox was very bored. He had nothing to do in his den. He wanted to go out and play, but his mother said it was too late. She said he had to sleep, because the night was dark and cold. The little fox did not want to sleep. He yawned and said, "Sleeping is not fun. I want to see the forest."

His mother said, "The forest is not safe at night. There are big and scary animals that can hurt you. You need to sleep, because sleeping is useful. It makes you grow and learn and be strong. Tomorrow, you can go out and play, when the sun is up and the forest is bright."

The little fox did not listen to his mother. He waited until she was asleep, and then he sneaked out of the den. He ran to the forest, and he felt very brave and curious. He saw many things that he had never seen before. He saw the moon and the stars, and he heard the owls and the crickets. He thought, "The forest is so beautiful and exciting. I am glad I came out."

But soon, he also saw things that he did not like. He saw the shadows and the noises, and he felt very cold and afraid. He saw the eyes and the teeth, and he heard the growls and the roars. He realized, "The forest is also very dangerous and scary. I wish I had stayed in the den."

He tried to run back to the den, but he did not know the way. He was lost and alone, and he cried for his mother. He hoped that she would hear him and come to find him. He learned, "Sleeping is not boring. It is useful and safe. I should have listened to my mother."

Luckily, his mother did hear him and came to find him. She was very angry and worried, but she was also very happy and relieved. She hugged him and took him back to the den. She said, "You were very naughty and foolish. You could have been hurt or eaten by the big and scary animals. You must never go out at night again. You must obey me and sleep when I tell you to."

The little fox said, "I am sorry, mother. I was wrong. I will never go out at night again. I will obey you and sleep when you tell me to. I love you, mother."

His mother said, "I love you, too, my little fox. Now, let us sleep, and dream of the forest."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents, they know what is best for you. Sleeping is useful and important for your health and happiness. The forest is beautiful and exciting, but also dangerous and scary. You should only explore it when it is safe and with someone who can protect you.

Lily was happy again and they mailed the painting to Mr. Fix-It. A few days later, they received the painting back in the mail. It was fixed and looked even better than before! Lily was so happy and she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me fix my painting!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a furry cat named Mittens. One day, Lily and Mittens went outside to play. They saw their friend Timmy and asked him to play too. 

Timmy said, "I can't play right now. I have to leave soon." 

Lily asked, "Can you stay and have some cocoa with us?" 

Timmy smiled and said, "Yes, I can stay for a little bit." 

They went inside and Lily's mom made them some cocoa. They all sat on the couch and drank their cocoa. Mittens even got a little bit of cocoa on his fur! 

After they finished their cocoa, Timmy had to leave. Lily said goodbye and Mittens meowed goodbye too. They had a fun day with their friend Timmy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the hot sun all day long. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time for his nap. Timmy didn't want to take a nap, he wanted to keep playing outside. But his mom said he needed to rest so he would have energy to play later.

Timmy went to his room and lay down, but he couldn't fall asleep. He kept thinking about all the fun he could be having outside. Suddenly, Timmy had an idea. He decided to store some of his energy for later, so he could play longer. He closed his eyes and took a nap.

When Timmy woke up, he felt refreshed and full of energy. He ran outside to play and had even more fun than before. Timmy learned that taking a nap was important and helped him have more fun later.

Lily and Max were excited. Mom said they could help her make a cake. They put on their aprons and washed their hands. Mom gave them a big bowl and a wooden spoon.

"Can I stir, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, you can stir, Lily. But be careful, don't spill the flour," Mom said.

Lily started to stir the flour and the sugar. She liked how the spoon made a sound in the bowl. Max watched her and waited for his turn.

"Can I stir, too, Mom?" Max asked.

"Of course, you can stir, too, Max. But let Lily finish first, okay?" Mom said.

Max nodded. He was a good brother. He waited until Lily said, "I'm done, Max. You can stir now."

Max took the spoon from Lily and began to stir. He stirred faster and faster. He wanted to make the cake quickly. He didn't see the flour flying out of the bowl.

"Max, slow down, you're making a mess!" Mom said.

Max looked around and saw the flour on the floor, on the table, and on the couch. He felt bad. He didn't mean to make a mess.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I was too excited," Max said.

"It's okay, Max. I know you were trying to help. But next time, stir gently, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. I'll stir gently next time," Max said.

Mom smiled and hugged Max and Lily. She said, "You're both good helpers. Now let's clean up and finish the cake."

Lily and Max helped Mom clean up the flour. Then they added the eggs, the milk, and the chocolate. They poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. They waited for the cake to bake. They could smell the chocolate in the air. They were excited. They loved cake.

"Good morning, Anna and Ben!" Mom says. "Time to get up and get ready for school. I have a surprise for you in the kitchen."

Anna and Ben rub their eyes and stretch. They love surprises. They jump out of their beds and run to the kitchen. Mom is waiting for them with a big smile.

"Look what I made for you!" Mom says. "Your favorite pastries! They are warm and sweet and yummy. Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Anna and Ben say. They sit at the table and grab a pastry each. They take a big bite and make happy noises.

"Thank you, Mom!" Anna and Ben say. "You are the best mom ever. You are so reliable. You always make us happy."

Mom hugs them and kisses them. She is proud of her twins. They are so polite and kind. She loves them very much.

"You are welcome, Anna and Ben!" Mom says. "You are the best twins ever. You are so smart and brave. I love you very much."

They finish their pastries and drink some milk. Then they brush their teeth and put on their clothes. They are ready for school. They grab their backpacks and follow Mom to the car. They wave goodbye and drive away. They are excited for a new day.

Sara and Ben went to the market with their mom. They liked to see all the different things people sold. Mom said they could choose one thing each to take home.

Sara saw a big basket of peppers. They were red, green, yellow and orange. She liked how they looked. She asked mom if she could have a pepper.

"Sure, you can have a pepper," mom said. "But you have to be polite and ask the seller first."

Sara nodded and walked to the basket. She said hello to the seller and pointed to a red pepper. "Can I have this one, please?" she asked.

The seller smiled and gave her the pepper. "Of course, you can. You are a very polite little girl. Here you go."

"Thank you very much," Sara said. She hugged the pepper and went back to mom.

Ben looked around the market. He did not want a pepper. He wanted something else. He saw a stall with toys. He saw a truck, a ball, a doll and a puzzle. He could not decide which one he liked best. He asked mom if he could have a toy.

"Sure, you can have a toy," mom said. "But you have to choose one. You can't have them all."

Ben nodded and walked to the stall. He looked at the toys again. He liked the truck, but he also liked the ball. He liked the doll, but he also liked the puzzle. He did not know which one to choose.

He asked the seller if he could play with the toys for a while. The seller said yes, but he had to be careful and not break them.

Ben played with the toys for a long time. He had fun with the truck, the ball, the doll and the puzzle. He liked them all. He did not want to choose one.

Mom came to the stall and said it was time to go. She asked Ben which toy he wanted to take home.

Ben looked at the toys. He looked at mom. He looked at Sara. Sara was holding her pepper. She looked happy.

Ben had an idea. He smiled and said, "I don't want a toy. I want a pepper, too."

Mom and the seller laughed. They said that was a good choice. They gave Ben a yellow pepper. He thanked them and hugged the pepper.

Sara and Ben were happy. They had chosen their peppers. They went home with mom. They showed dad their peppers. Dad said they were very smart and very polite. He said he would make them a pepper soup for dinner. Sara and Ben said they would help him. They loved their peppers. They loved their mom and dad. They loved each other.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They had a big sack full of toys. They liked to share their toys with other children.

"Look, there is a new boy on the swing," Lily said. "He looks sad. Maybe he wants to play with us."

Tom got off the swing and followed Lily and Ben. They opened their sack and showed him their toys. There were cars, dolls, balls, books, and puzzles.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play at the beach. They make sand castles and look for shells. One day, they see a big boat on the water. It is dull and gray. It makes a loud noise.

"Look, Ben, a boat!" Sara says. She points at the boat.

"I don't like it. It is ugly and noisy. It scares the fish and the birds." Ben says. He frowns.

Sara and Ben start to argue. Sara thinks the boat is interesting and wants to watch it. Ben thinks the boat is bad and wants to ignore it. They stop playing and start shouting.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom says. She comes to the beach with a basket. "It is time for lunch. Come and eat."

Sara and Ben stop arguing. They are hungry and tired. They follow Mom to the picnic spot. They see sandwiches, fruit, and juice in the basket. They smile.

"Can we share, Sara?" Ben asks.

"Of course, Ben. We are twins. We can share everything." Sara says.

They hug and say sorry. They eat and drink. They feel better. They look at the boat again. It is still dull and gray. It still makes a loud noise. But they don't mind. They have each other. They have fun. They love the beach.

Tim and Anna liked to play with their toy bow and arrow. They pretended to be brave hunters in the forest. They took turns to shoot at a big tree.

"Look, I hit the tree!" Tim said, pointing at his arrow.

"Good job, Tim! Now it's my turn!" Anna said, taking the bow.

She pulled the string and let go. But the arrow flew past the tree and hit a bird. The bird fell to the ground.

"Oh no!" Anna cried. "I hurt the bird!"

She ran to the bird and picked it up. It was still alive, but it looked miserable. It had a wound on its wing.

"I'm sorry, bird. I didn't mean to hurt you," Anna said, stroking its feathers.

"Anna, what did you do?" Tim asked, joining her.

"I shot the bird with the arrow. It was an accident," Anna said, tears in her eyes.

"You have to be careful with the arrow, Anna. You can't shoot at living things. You have to mind what you aim at," Tim said.

"I know, Tim. I was stupid. Can we help the bird?" Anna asked.

"Maybe we can. Let's take it to Mom. She knows how to fix things," Tim said.

They carried the bird to their house and showed it to their mom. She was surprised and worried.

"What happened, kids?" she asked.

"We were playing with the bow and arrow, and Anna shot the bird," Tim explained.

"Oh, Anna. That was very wrong. You have to be gentle with animals. They have feelings too," Mom said.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't want to hurt the bird. I love birds," Anna said.

"I know, honey. But you have to be more careful. Let me see the bird. Maybe I can help it," Mom said.

She took the bird and removed the arrow. She cleaned the wound and wrapped it with a bandage. She gave the bird some water and seeds.

"There, there. You'll be okay, little bird. You just need some rest and love," Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. You're the best," Tim and Anna said.

They watched the bird in a cage. It looked less miserable. It chirped softly.

"Can we keep the bird, Mom?" Anna asked.

"No, sweetie. The bird belongs to the wild. We have to let it go when it gets better. But we can visit it and feed it until then," Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. We'll take good care of the bird. And we'll never shoot at living things again. Right, Tim?" Anna said.

"Right, Anna. We'll mind what we aim at. And we'll be kind to animals," Tim said.

They hugged Mom and the bird. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and gentle with their toy bow and arrow. And they made a new friend in the bird.

Lily and Ben were excited to bake a cake with Mom. They put on their aprons and washed their hands. Mom showed them how to mix the flour, sugar, eggs and milk in a big bowl. Lily and Ben took turns to stir the batter with a wooden spoon.

"Can I add the chocolate chips?" Lily asked.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said.

"Of course, you can both add some chocolate chips. But not too many, or the cake will be too sweet," Mom said. She gave them each a small cup of chocolate chips and helped them sprinkle them over the batter.

Mom poured the batter into a round pan and put it in the oven. She set the timer and told Lily and Ben to be careful and not touch the oven, because it was very hot.

"Now we have to wait for the cake to bake. It will take about half an hour. What can we do while we wait?" Mom asked.

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They decided to play with their toys in the living room. They brought their dolls, cars, blocks and books and had fun making stories and noises. They also cleaned up their mess when they were done.

Ding! The timer rang and Mom called them to the kitchen.

"The cake is ready! Let's take it out of the oven and let it cool down a bit," Mom said. She used oven mitts to take out the pan and put it on a rack. The cake smelled delicious and looked golden and fluffy.

Lily and Ben clapped their hands and cheered. They were so happy to see their cake. Mom smiled and hugged them.

"You did a great job, Lily and Ben. You are such good helpers. Now, let's decorate the cake with some frosting and sprinkles. Then we can cut a slice for each of us and enjoy it. How does that sound?" Mom asked.

Lily and Ben nodded eagerly. They followed Mom to the table, where she had prepared some frosting, sprinkles, a knife and a spatula. They helped Mom spread the frosting over the cake and sprinkle some colorful dots on top. They admired their work and felt proud.

"Wow, our cake looks amazing! Can we eat it now, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, we can. But first, let's put the cake in a safe place, so that our dog Spot doesn't get to it. He loves chocolate, but it's not good for him. We'll put the cake on the top shelf of the cupboard, where he can't reach it. Then we'll wash our hands again and get some plates and forks," Mom said.

Lily and Ben agreed. They helped Mom put the cake in a safe place and wash their hands. Then they got some plates and forks and sat down at the table. Mom cut a slice of cake for each of them and put it on their plates. They thanked Mom and took a bite of their cake.

"Mmm, this is so yummy! Thank you, Mom, for baking with us. We love you!" Lily and Ben said.

"I love you too, Lily and Ben. You are very welcome. This is the best cake ever, because we made it together," Mom said.

They smiled and hugged each other. They enjoyed their cake and felt very happy. They had a wonderful time baking with Mom.

Lily says, "We need to use the curved tracks. The curved tracks can bend. We can put them together to make a circle. I will show you."

Lily and Ben start to make the loop. They use the curved tracks and some straight tracks. They make a big circle on the floor. They put a train on the loop. They turn on the train. The train starts to move. It goes round and round the loop.

Lily and Ben watch the train. They clap their hands. They say, "Wow, this is interesting. The train is fast. It does not stop. It does not fall off. It is fun to watch."

They play with the loop for a long time. They try different trains. They make the loop bigger and smaller. They have a lot of fun.

Lily and Ben are happy. They like the loop. They think it is a good way to play with trains. They recommend the loop to their other friends. They say, "You should try the loop. It is interesting and fun. You will like it."

Ben and Lily are twins. They share a room and a bed. Every night, they drink some milk before they sleep. They like milk. It makes them warm and happy.

One night, Ben wakes up. He is thirsty. He looks for his milk cup. But his cup is empty. He sees Lily's cup. It is full of milk. He wants to drink it.

He reaches for Lily's cup. But Lily wakes up too. She sees Ben. She says, "No, Ben! That is my milk! You have your own milk!"

Ben says, "But my milk is gone! I am thirsty! Please, Lily, can I have some of your milk?"

Lily thinks. She loves Ben. He is her brother. She says, "OK, Ben. You can have some of my milk. But not all of it. I am thirsty too."

Ben smiles. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. I love you."

He drinks some of Lily's milk. He gives her back the cup. They hug. They say, "Good night."

Lily picked up a short stick and said, "No, I have a wand! I can do magic and make things happen!" She waved the stick and said some silly words.

They got angry and tried to take each other's stick. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They were not having fun anymore.

Then, a friendly dog came over and sniffed the sticks. He wagged his tail and barked. He wanted to play with them. He looked at Ben and Lily with his big eyes and licked their faces.

Ben and Lily stopped fighting and smiled. They realized they were being silly. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to share their sticks and play with the dog.

They threw the sticks and the dog ran after them. He brought them back and waited for more. Ben and Lily laughed and clapped. They had a new friend.

They played until it was time to go home. They thanked the dog and gave him a pat. They said goodbye to each other and promised to play again soon. They learned that sticks can be many things, but the best thing is to have fun with them.
