Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the yard. They have a ball, a bike and a dog. The dog is big and brown. His name is Rex.

One day, a new boy comes to the yard. He is unknown. He has a red hat and a blue shirt. He says hello to Tom and Sam. He asks if he can play with them.

Tom and Sam do not like the new boy. They think he is strange. They do not want to share their toys. They start to tease the new boy. They call him names. They take his hat and throw it away. They kick his bike. They laugh at him.

The new boy is sad and angry. He wants his hat and his bike back. He does not like Tom and Sam. He sees Rex. He has an idea. He runs to Rex and grabs his tail. He pulls it hard.

Rex is hurt and scared. He does not like the new boy. He barks and growls. He turns around and bites the new boy. He bites his arm and his leg. He makes him bleed.

From that day on, Lily kept drawing and printing her pictures, and she always remembered the lesson her mom taught her.

The creature was a little mouse. It nodded its head as if to say hello to Sally. Surprised but excited, Sally smiled and nodded back. The mouse then scurried off deeper into the tunnel and Sally followed it.

The mouse showed Sally lots of wonderful things in the tunnel. They both had so much fun exploring and discovering new treasures. Eventually, they reached the end of the tunnel, and Sally said goodbye to her new friend. She was sad to leave but was glad she'd made such a nice friend.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful dragon. He lay peacefully in his cave with his back against the wall, sleeping. Suddenly, he felt a rumbling in the distance and opened his eyes. He saw zero creatures in sight, but he could feel them getting closer. They were loud and powerful, and he knew he had to defend himself.

The dragon lay still but kept an eye out for the creatures. Suddenly, one appeared from around the corner! It was a small creature, with wings and bright blue eyes. The dragon was surprised but ready to fight. He let out a powerful growl and the creature backed away.

Suddenly, more of the creatures appeared! There were five of them, all in a line. The dragon lay quietly and watched them carefully. He knew they were no match for the powerful dragon. He roared loudly, and they ran away, never to be seen again.

The dragon lay down in his cave and went back to sleep, feeling safe and secure. From that day forward, no creatures ever came near the dragon again.

They were both curious and adventurous, and they both loved the woods. They hugged each other and smiled. They were happy to be twins and friends.

"Ben, Anna doesn't need a license for her toy car. It's not a real car. It's a toy car. You can't take it from her. It's hers. You have to share and be nice," Mommy says.

She lit a match and moved it closer to the flower. But the flower did not like the fire. It started to turn brown and curl up. The fire also caught the curtain and the wall. Lily was scared. She dropped the match and ran out of the room. She screamed for her mom and dad.

Her mom and dad heard her and came running. They saw the fire and grabbed a bucket of water. They threw the water on the fire and put it out. They were angry and sad. They hugged Lily and told her she was very naughty. They said fire was dangerous and could hurt her and the house. They said she could never play with matches again.

Lily felt sorry and cried. She said she was sorry and she did not mean to burn the flower and the house. She said she only wanted to make the flower more beautiful. Her mom and dad said they loved her, but she had to learn her lesson. They said they would buy her a new flower, but it would be a fake one. They said it would be mild and safe and would not burn. Lily nodded and said she would be good. She hoped the new flower would be as pretty as the old one.

Sam felt hurt and angry. He did not like Tom's words. He felt embarrassed and alone.

"Wow, look at that vehicle, mom!" Lila said. "It's so cool! I want to see it up close!"

Sara stopped crying and smiled. She thanked her mom and hugged the dress. She said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I can't wait to show Leo his new dress. He will love it." Her mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Sara. I'm glad you're happy. Let's go home and play with Leo." They left the toy store and went home. Sara and Leo had a lot of fun with the new dress. They forgot about the gloomy cashier.

Max came over and looked at the bug. It had six legs and two wings. It was shiny and pretty.

Max hugged Lily and tried to make her feel better.

"I'm sorry, Lily. It was a bad bug. It was not nice. Let me see your finger," he said.

He looked at Lily's finger and saw a small red mark. He kissed it and said, "There, there. It will be okay. Do you want a band-aid?"

Lily nodded and sniffed. She held Max's hand and they went inside to find their mom. She gave Lily a band-aid and a hug. She told them to be careful with bugs and to wash their hands. Lily and Ben are friends who live next door to each other. They like to play in their gardens and look at the flowers and trees. One day, Lily sees a big sunflower in Ben's garden. It is taller than her and has a bright yellow face.

"Wow, Ben, your sunflower is so big and pretty!" Lily says. "How did it grow so fast?"

Ben smiles and says, "I planted a seed in the spring and watered it every day. Then the sun came and helped it grow. Do you want to see the seed packet?"

Lily nods and follows Ben to his shed. He shows her a packet with a picture of a sunflower and some words. Lily cannot read the words, but she likes the picture.

"Can I have a seed too, Ben?" Lily asks. "I want to grow a sunflower in my garden."

Ben thinks for a moment. He likes his sunflower, but he also likes Lily. He decides to share his seeds with her. He gives her two seeds and says, "Here you go, Lily. You can plant them in your garden and water them every day. Maybe they will grow as big as mine."

Lily is very happy and thanks Ben. She runs to her garden and digs two holes. She puts a seed in each hole and covers them with dirt. She gets a watering can and waters them gently. She hopes they will grow soon.

But not everyone is happy. Tom, who lives across the street, sees Lily and Ben planting seeds. He is envious of their sunflowers. He does not have any seeds or flowers in his garden. He only has weeds and rocks. He thinks of a way to spoil their fun.

That night, when Lily and Ben are asleep, Tom sneaks into their gardens. He finds the seeds that Lily planted and pulls them out. He throws them away and laughs. He thinks he is very clever and mean.

But he does not see the news that is waiting for him in the morning. When he wakes up, he looks out of his window and sees something amazing. The seeds that he threw away did not die. They landed on his lawn and started to grow. Now he has two sunflowers in his garden, bigger and brighter than Lily and Ben's. He is very surprised and confused.

Lily and Ben also wake up and look out of their windows. They see that their seeds are gone and feel very sad. They wonder who took them and why. They go outside and see Tom's sunflowers. They are very angry and hurt.

"Tom, did you take our seeds?" Lily asks.

Tom does not know what to say. He feels ashamed and sorry. He knows he did a bad thing.

"Yes, I did," he says. "I was envious of your sunflowers. I wanted to have some too. But I did not know they would grow in my garden. I am sorry, Lily and Ben. Can you forgive me?"

Lily and Ben look at each other. They are still upset, but they also see that Tom is sorry. They decide to forgive him. They are good friends.

"It's okay, Tom," Ben says. "We forgive you. But you have to promise not to do it again. And you have to share your sunflowers with us."

Tom nods and says, "I promise. And I will share my sunflowers with you. They are too big for me anyway. Maybe we can all play in our gardens and look at the flowers and trees."

Lily and Ben smile and say, "That sounds like fun. Let's do that."

They all go to Tom's garden and admire his sunflowers. They also see some other seeds that have sprouted on his lawn. They wonder what they will grow into. They are excited and curious.

They have learned a lesson about growing, news and being envious. They have also learned about friendship and forgiveness. They are happy.

Anna and Ben liked to play in the woods. They liked to climb trees, find bugs, and make forts. One day, they saw a big log on the ground. It was long and thick and brown.

"Let's use this log for our fort!" Ben said. "We can roll it to our spot and make a wall."

"Good idea!" Anna said. "But it looks heavy. How can we move it?"

They tried to push the log, but it did not move. They tried to pull the log, but it did not move. They tried to lift the log, but it was too heavy.

"This log is not useful!" Anna said. "It is too big and too heavy. Let's find another one."

But Ben did not want to give up. He had an idea. He saw a stick on the ground. It was long and thin and strong.

"Look, Anna!" Ben said. "We can use this stick to move the log. We can put it under the log and make a lever. Then we can push the stick and the log will roll."

Anna did not understand. She did not know what a lever was. She thought Ben was silly.

"That will not work!" Anna said. "That stick is too small and too weak. It will break. Let's go, Ben. This log is not worth it."

But Ben did not listen. He put the stick under the log and pushed hard. He hoped the stick would not break. He hoped the log would roll.

And it did!

The stick did not break. The log did roll. It rolled fast and far. It rolled down the hill and into the road. It rolled in front of a car.

The car saw the log and stopped. The driver was angry. He got out of the car and shouted.

"Who did this? Who put this log in the road? This is dangerous! This is stupid!"

Anna and Ben heard the shout. They were scared. They hid behind a tree. They did not want to be seen. They did not want to be in trouble.

They learned a lesson. They learned that some logs are not useful. They learned that some ideas are not good. They learned that some games are not fun. They learned to stop and think before they act.

Lila and Sam were twins who liked to go to the harbor with their dad. They loved to see the big boats and the fish and the birds. Sometimes they would help their dad with his work. He was a diver who fixed things under the water.

One day, their dad told them he had a special job to do. He had to find a lost ring that a lady had dropped from her boat. He said it was very deep and dark under the water, and he needed a special suit and a tank to breathe. He asked Lila and Sam if they wanted to learn how to dive with him.

Lila and Sam were very excited. They said yes, yes, yes! They wanted to learn how to dive and see the ring and the things under the water. Their dad smiled and said they had to be very brave and careful. He gave them each a small suit and a mask and a snorkel. He said they could only go a little bit under the water, and they had to stay close to him.

They put on their suits and masks and snorkels and followed their dad to the edge of the harbor. He jumped in first and waved at them. Then Lila and Sam jumped in too. They felt the cold water on their skin and the bubbles in their mouth. They looked around and saw the blue water and the green plants and the colorful fish. They saw their dad go deeper and deeper, until he was a small dot.

Lila and Sam stayed near the surface and played with the fish and the plants. They were having fun, but they also wondered what their dad was doing. They hoped he would find the ring and come back soon. They did not see the big shadow that was moving under them. It was a shark that was hungry and curious. It saw the twins and decided to take a closer look. It swam faster and faster, until it was almost under them.

Suddenly, their dad came back. He had the ring in his hand. He saw the shark and shouted at Lila and Sam. He told them to swim to the boat, fast, fast, fast! He grabbed a stick and hit the shark on the nose. The shark was angry and scared. It turned around and swam away. Lila and Sam swam to the boat and climbed on board. They were scared and happy. "That's a rubber ball, Lily. It's made of a special material that can stretch and bounce. Do you want to play with it?" her mom said, smiling.

"Yes, please!" Lily said, excited. She threw the ball on the floor and watched it bounce back to her. She giggled and threw it again. She liked how it felt in her hand, soft and smooth.

She decided to examine it more closely. She squeezed it hard and saw it change shape. She pulled it and saw it stretch. She rubbed it on her hair and saw it stick. She was amazed by the ball. She thought it was a very clever toy.

Her dad looked up from his computer and saw her. He smiled and said, "Hello, Lily. What do you have there?"

"Lily, that was not a good idea. You broke my computer. That was very naughty," he said, sternly.

Lily felt sorry and scared. She did not mean to break his computer. She just wanted to show him the ball. She started to cry and said, "I'm sorry, dad. I didn't know. I was just examining the ball. Please don't be mad at me."

Her dad sighed and hugged her. He was not really mad at her. He knew she was curious and thoughtful. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you didn't mean it. But you have to be careful with your toys. Lily nodded and said, "Yes, dad. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you."

Her dad said, "I love you too, Lily. Now, why don't you go and play with your ball outside? It's a nice day. And maybe you can find some other things to examine. But be gentle and safe, okay?"

Lily said, "Okay, dad. Thank you. Bye!" She took her ball and ran outside. She was happy again. She still liked to examine things. But she also learned to be careful and respectful. She was a good girl.

They ate and drank and talked about their adventure. Lily was very happy. She had a good day and a good friend.

But then, she felt something wet in her pocket. She reached in and pulled out the pearl. It was not a pearl anymore. It was a drop of water.

Lily gasped and looked at the oyster. It was not an oyster anymore. It was a shell. The oyster had gone away.

Lily felt sad and angry. She had lost her pearl. She threw the shell on the ground and started to weep.

"Why are you weeping, Lily?" Tom asked, worried.

"My pearl, my pearl, it is gone!" Lily cried. "The oyster took it back!"

Tom felt sorry for Lily. He did not know what to do. He wanted to make her feel better.

He looked around and saw another oyster on the sand. He picked it up and opened it with a rock. He saw another shiny thing inside.

He gave it to Lily and said, "Here, Lily, have this pearl. It is yours. I found it for you."

Lily stopped weeping and looked at the pearl. It was bigger and brighter than the first one. She smiled and took it from Tom. She thanked him and hugged him.

She put the pearl in her pocket and hoped it would stay. She felt happy again. She had a good day and a good friend.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck in the park. The truck has oil in it. The oil is for the cars.

"Look, a big truck!" Tom says. "Let's go see it!"

"OK, but be careful," Jen says. "The oil is not for us."

They run to the truck. The truck driver is not there. He is in the shop. Tom and Jen climb on the truck. They see a big hose. The hose has oil in it.

"Stop, Tom, stop!" Jen says. "You are making a mess!"

"Tom, you are bad!" Jen says. She is angry and sad. She is covered in oil. She tries to wipe it off. But it does not come off.

Then, they hear a loud noise. It is the truck driver. He is back. He sees the oil. He sees Tom and Jen. He is very mad.

"What did you do?" he yells. "You ruined my truck! You ruined the park! You are in big trouble!"

He grabs Tom and Jen. He takes them to the shop. He calls their parents. Their parents are very mad too. They come to the park. They see the oil. They see Tom and Jen. They are very disappointed.

"Tom, Jen, how could you?" they say. "You did a bad thing. You hurt the park. You hurt the animals. You hurt yourselves. You have to say sorry. You have to clean up. You have to pay for the damage."

Tom and Jen learn a lesson. They learn to be careful. They learn to respect the truck. They learn to respect the oil. They learn to respect the park. They learn to respect the driver. They learn to respect their parents.

But it is too late. The park is not the same. The oil is not gone. The animals are not happy. The flowers are not pretty. The truck is not working. The driver is not happy. The parents are not proud.

Tom and Jen are not friends. They are sad. They are lonely. They are sorry.

Lily stopped crying and smiled. She said thank you and yes. She said he was very kind and friendly. He said she was too. They walked to Miss Lee and asked for a band-aid. Miss Lee gave them one and said they were very brave and polite. She said they could sit next to each other on the rug.

She picked up the thing and held it in her hand. She said, "Hello, what are you? Are you a bug? Do you have a name?" The thing did not answer. It tried to bite Lily's finger. Lily felt a sharp pain. She dropped the thing and cried.

Mama heard Lily's cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw the thing on the ground. She said, "Lily, that is an ant. Ants are not nice to hold. They can hurt you. You should not touch them. You should leave them alone."

Lily was sad and sorry. She said, "I did not know, Mama. I wanted to learn about the ant. I did not want to hurt it or make it angry. I thought it was a friend."

Mama hugged Lily and said, "I know, Lily. You are curious and smart. But some things are not safe to learn by yourself. You should always ask me or Daddy before you touch something you do not know. We can help you learn in a good way."

Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mama. I will do that. I am sorry for the ant. I hope it is okay." Mama said, "It is okay, Lily. The ant will find its way back to its home. But you should be careful next time. Ants are not nice to play with." Lily said, "I understand, Mama. I will be careful." Mama kissed Lily and said, "I love you, Lily. You are my good girl." Lily said, "I love you too, Mama. You are my nice Mama."

The Goose tilted its head and quacked.

"I'm sure you have a name," Lucy said. She smiled and gave the goose a pat.

The Goose quacked again and shook its head.

Lucy noticed a light twinkle in the Goose's eye. She smiled and said, "Well, I'm going to call you Goosey then. That's a nice name, right?"

The Goose seemed to agree and quacked once more. Lucy laughed and said goodbye, and went skipping away, excited to tell her family about her new friend.

The two friends returned to the pond, happy and full. John was even less lazy than before, and he never forgot the fun adventure he had with Isabelle.

They heard their mom coming and got scared. They tried to hide the salt, but it was too late. Mom saw the mess and was angry. She asked them what they were doing and why they wasted the salt. She told them that salt was not a toy, but a food that made other foods taste better. She also told them that salt was precious and hard to get. She said that people who lived near the sea had to work hard to collect the salt from the water. She said that people who lived far from the sea had to trade other things for the salt. She said that salt was a gift from God and they should be thankful and respectful.

Sara and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They apologized to their mom and helped her clean the table. They learned their lesson and never played with salt again. They also learned to be curious, but not careless. They learned to value what they had and not waste it. They learned to listen to their mom and obey her. They were tired after their adventure, but they were also wiser and happier.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and smell them. Lily saw a big red rose and ran to it. She wanted to pick it and give it to Ben.

But when she reached the rose, she saw a fairy sitting on it. The fairy was very small and had wings. She was holding a wand and smiled at Lily.

"Hello, little girl," the fairy said. "Do you like roses?"

Lily was surprised and scared. She had never seen a fairy before. She nodded and said, "Yes, I like roses. They are pretty and smell good."

The fairy nodded and said, "Roses are special flowers. They have magic in them. They can make people happy and peaceful. Do you want to see?"

Lily was curious and said, "Yes, please."

The fairy waved her wand and said, "Abracadabra!" Suddenly, many roses appeared in the garden. They were of different colors and sizes. They filled the air with their fragrance.

Lily and Ben were amazed and happy. They ran around and touched the roses. They felt peaceful and joyful.

The fairy smiled and said, "I hope you enjoy the roses. They are a gift from me. But remember, be kind to them and to each other. They will only last for a day. Then they will disappear."

Lily and Ben thanked the fairy and hugged her. They said, "Thank you, fairy. You are very nice. We will be kind to the roses and to each other. We will never forget you."

The fairy hugged them back and said, "You are very welcome, children. You are very sweet. I will never forget you either. Goodbye and have fun."

The fairy flew away and disappeared. Lily and Ben played with the roses until the sun set. They felt peaceful and happy. They had a magical day.

The moral of the story is: Never lose hope, even when you are in a bad situation. There is always something beautiful and good in the world. Friendship can help you overcome any obstacle.

Sara nods. She understands. "So, the clock tells us when it is noon or night?"

Tom shrugs. He is not sure. He points at the clock. "Look, the big hand is on the twelve and the small hand is on the twelve. Maybe that means it is noon."

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys. Tom had a box of matches and Lily had a doll. Tom liked to make fire with the matches, but Lily was scared of fire.

"Look, Lily, I can make fire!" Tom said, as he struck a match on the box.

"Stop it, Tom, fire is bad!" Lily said, as she hugged her doll. "Fire can burn things and hurt people!"

"No, fire is good! Fire is fun and warm and bright!" Tom said, as he held the match close to his face.

Lily saw that Tom had no hair on his head. He was bald. She had an idea.

"Tom, do you want hair?" Lily asked, as she took a strand of her doll's hair.

"What? Hair? How?" Tom asked, as he looked at Lily.

"Here, I can give you hair. Just accept this." Lily said, as she tried to stick the doll's hair on Tom's head.

"Hey, stop that! That's not hair, that's doll hair!" Tom said, as he pushed Lily away. "That doesn't match me, that matches your doll!"

Tom and Lily started to fight over the doll and the matches. They pulled and pushed and shouted and cried. Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"What are you two doing?" Mom asked, as she saw the mess. "Why are you fighting?"

Tom and Lily stopped fighting and looked at Mom. They felt sorry and ashamed.

"Tom was playing with fire and I was scared. I tried to give him hair, but he didn't like it." Lily said, as she sniffed.

"Lily was sticking doll hair on my head and I didn't want it. I wanted to play with fire, but she didn't let me." Tom said, as he rubbed his eyes.

Mom sighed and hugged them both.

"Tom, fire is dangerous. You can't play with matches. You could hurt yourself or others. You have to be careful and listen to Lily." Mom said, as she took the matches away.

"Lily, Tom is bald and that's okay. You can't force him to have hair. You have to respect his choice and be nice to him." Mom said, as she gave the doll back.

Tom and Lily nodded and said sorry to each other. They hugged and made up.

"Can we play something else?" Tom asked, as he smiled.

"Sure, what do you want to play?" Lily asked, as she smiled back.

Mom smiled too and watched them play. She was glad they learned to accept each other and their differences.

Lila was a camel who lived in the desert. She liked to go to the oasis with her friends, where they could drink water and eat grass. One day, she saw a new camel at the oasis. He was big and brown, with a long neck and a hump. Lila thought he was ugly.

"Who are you?" she asked him.

"I am Omar," he said. "I came from far away. I am looking for a new home."

Lila did not want him to stay. She said, "You are ugly. You do not belong here. Go away."

Omar felt sad. He said, "I am sorry. I did not mean to bother you. I just need some water and food. I have been walking for a long time."

Lila did not care. She said, "Go away. Go away. Go away."

Omar turned around and walked away. He did not know where to go. He was thirsty and hungry and tired.

Lila felt proud. She said to her friends, "I made him go away. He was ugly. He did not belong here."

Her friends did not agree. They said, "Lila, you were mean. He was not ugly. He was different. He needed help. You should have been kind."

Lila did not listen. She said, "I do not care. He was ugly. He did not belong here."

The next day, Lila went to the oasis again. But she did not find water or grass. She found sand and rocks. The oasis was gone. A big wind had blown it away.

Lila was shocked. She said, "Where is the oasis? Where is the water? Where is the grass?"

Her friends said, "The oasis is gone. The wind took it away. We have to find a new one."

Lila was scared. She said, "How will we find a new one? We do not know where to go. We will die of thirst and hunger."

Her friends said, "Maybe Omar knows. He came from far away. He may have seen other oases. Let us go and find him. Maybe he will help us."

Lila felt ashamed. She said, "But I was mean to him. I told him to go away. I called him ugly. He will not help us."

Her friends said, "You were mean, but you can say sorry. You can be kind. You can be his friend. Maybe he will forgive you."

Lila realized she was wrong. She said, "You are right. I was mean, but I can say sorry. I can be kind. I can be his friend. Maybe he will forgive me."

So Lila and her friends went to look for Omar. They hoped he would help them. They hoped he would be their friend.

The moral of the story is: Do not judge others by their looks. Be kind and helpful to those in need. You never know when you may need their help.

One villager came up with a clever idea. He told the villagers to dig a big hole, far away from the village. They started to dig, and soon, they had finished their work. 

The villagers connected a pipe from the lake to the hole and opened the valve. The water from the lake started to run through the pipe and into the hole. The villagers cheered as the extra water drained away from the lake, leaving it to its former state. 

The villagers learned an important lesson from this experience. They learned that being angry won't solve anything. Instead, they need to come up with clever solutions to solve their problems.

Suddenly, he heard a loud rumble. It was an elephant! The elephant didn't like the monkey messing with his tree. He started running as fast as he could, but the elephant was too fast and caught him.

"You are a foolish monkey," the elephant said. "You shouldn't have gone into my tree without asking me first." 

The elephant then lifted the monkey and threw him away, into the bushes. The monkey was never seen again. 

Moral of the story: always be careful to not do foolish things and always ask permission before entering someone's tree!

Once upon a time there was a bear named Gizmo. He loved exploring the forest, but he was a bit clumsy. As he was wandering around, he began to feel the ground tremble beneath his feet. He looked around to see who else was shaking, but all the other animals were calmly standing still. Gizmo realized that he was feeling an earthquake and became very scared.

Gizmo ran quickly to find a safe place, but the shaking of the earth kept following him. Everywhere he looked, he could see the trees shaking. He was so scared that he didn't even notice when he stumbled and fell over. He lay there trembling until he heard a voice.

"Gizmo! Are you ok?" The voice belonged to Gizmo's friend, a rabbit named Hippo. He helped Gizmo up and explained that the trembling was part of an earthquake. Impressed by the power of this natural force, Gizmo thanked Hippo for helping him understand what was happening.

"There is great power in nature," Hippo said. "It's important to remember that even when something looks scary, it can still be a beautiful thing." Gizmo learned an important lesson that day: respect nature, and it will keep you safe.

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course we can. Let's unlock it."

Tom and his mom walked through the gate and explored the town. Tom was so excited to see the shops, the parks and the animals. Everywhere he went, he found something new and exciting.

He didn't know what it was, but he followed the sound. After walking a long way, he saw an old saw on the ground. He was curious and tried to pick it up and take it home with him.

But just as he was about to touch it, the saw started to speak! "Please don't touch me," the saw said. "But why?" the boy asked, surprised.

"You see," the saw said, "I was once a long and powerful saw, but I grew careless and stopped taking care of myself. Now I am rusty and worn, because I didn't take care of myself. The small boy was taken aback. He thanked the saw for the warning, and ran home with the lesson ringing in his ears. He remembered the saw's advice and from that day on, he took good care of himself.

A few minutes later he came back, buzzing softly. He had brought all of his bee friends, who buzzed around her in a big circle. The sound made her feel better, and the little girl smiled for the first time in a long time. The bee's friends flew away and the little girl stopped weeping. 

The grass was a happy place for her once again, and she visited it every day to feel better. 

She never forgot the kind bees, who showed her that even shy little girls could come out of their shells with a little help from their friends.

After a while, Lily's mom called her over to go home. She said goodbye to the boy and ran home with the wind blowing behind her. When she got home, she told her mom about her fun day at the park. She couldn't wait to go back and play with her new friend again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside and eat carrots. One day, Benny was playing in the forest when he saw a big, scary wolf. The wolf wanted to eat Benny for dinner!

Benny was very scared because he knew the wolf was difficult to beat. Benny remembered what his mommy had told him: "If you ever feel scared, remember that I love you and I will always protect you." 

Benny closed his eyes and thought about his mommy's words. Suddenly, he felt a warm feeling in his heart. He knew his mommy was watching over him and would protect him from the wolf. 

With a burst of courage, Benny hopped away from the wolf and ran back to his mommy. Benny was safe and sound, thanks to the love and protection of his mommy. The moral of the story is that love and protection can help us overcome difficult situations.

The bird and the cat played the game. The cat won the game. The cat opened the cage. The cat caught the bird. The bird was very sad. The end.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing outside. They saw a big, rough rock. The cat had an idea. "Let's spin around the rock!" said the cat. The dog liked the idea and they both started to spin.

As they spun, the cat's tail got stuck in a zip on the dog's coat. They both stopped spinning and tried to get free. The cat was scared and the dog was sad. They did not know what to do.

A bird saw them and wanted to help. The bird flew down and used its beak to open the zip. The cat and the dog were free! They were so happy and thanked the bird. From that day on, they all played together and became the best of friends.

One day, a little girl named Mia went for a walk with her mom. They walked through the park and saw many different things. They saw birds, trees, and flowers. Mia liked to look at all the different colors.

As they walked, Mia saw something strange on the ground. It was a skull. She asked her mom, "What is this?" Her mom told her it was a skull from a small animal. Mia was very interested and wanted to observe it.

Mia looked at the skull carefully. She saw that it had two holes for the eyes and a hole for the nose. She thought it looked different from anything she had ever seen before. Mia and her mom talked about the skull and how it was once part of an animal. After learning about it, they continued their walk, looking for more interesting things to observe.

The loud bird flew high in the sky to tell everyone about the emergency. The fast squirrel ran to tell all the animals in the forest. The tall tree waved its branches to show everyone where to go. Bow and his friends worked together to help everyone.

Soon, the big, dark cloud came and brought lots of rain. But, all the animals were safe in their homes, thanks to Bow and his friends. After the rain stopped, the sun came out and the forest was beautiful again.

Max tried one last time. He closed his eyes and said a wish for the clouds. Then he jumped as high as he could and blinked his eyes. Suddenly, Max felt something soft on his face. It was a fluffy white cloud! Smiling, Max opened his eyes and finally touched his wish.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters. The older sister was very nosy. She always wanted to know what her younger sister was doing.

One day, the younger sister was playing outside. The older sister looked out the window and saw her. "What are you doing?" She asked.

The younger sister looked up and smiled. "I'm playing!" She said.

"What are you playing?" The older sister asked again.

The younger sister just smiled and nodded her head. She didn't want to tell her nosy sister what she was doing. 

The older sister was very frustrated, but she couldn't get the younger sister to tell her. She knew she wouldn't get an answer, so she gave up and went back inside.

The younger sister was glad she was able to keep her secret. She kept on playing and smiled the whole time.

Once upon a time there was a man. He wanted to build something very special. So he collected some hard celery from the garden. He was very determined to build something out of the celery.

He thought for a long time about what he could build. He finally had an idea and went to work. He started to cut and shape the celery into different shapes and sizes. He kept going until he had all the pieces he needed to build his special creation.

The man worked very hard until he was finished. He proudly looked at what he had made. It was a big and beautiful celery castle! He was so proud of himself because he had built something so wonderful.

He carefully put the castle on the ground. He wanted the whole world to see his amazing work. And so he did. The people who saw the castle were amazed at what the man had built. They said it was the most beautiful celery castle they had ever seen!

Once there was a clever crocodile. He wanted to do something special. So he decided to build a sandcastle. He used his hands and a lot of sand to make a big castle. He added some shells to make it look even better. He was really proud of his work.

The crocodile was not sad though. They both spent the day exploring the sandcastle. They found a lot of interesting things, like some colorful stones and a shiny stick. They laughed and had so much fun!

At the end of the day the clever crocodile was glad that he had done such a special thing. He and the seal were very happy with their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Kay. She was very stubborn and would always insist on having her own way.

One day Kay was outside playing when she suddenly saw an old key in the grass. She stopped playing and picked up the key. She looked around and no one was in sight.

She wanted to keep the key, so she quickly put it in her pocket. But then a big, scary man approached Kay. He wanted to take the key from her. He said it was his, but Kay kept insisting that it was her key.

The man got angrier and angrier, and soon it became very gloomy. Kay was very scared and started to cry. But suddenly, the man backed away and left. Kay was relieved and hugged her key tightly.

The key belonged to Kay and she was determined to keep it forever!

Once upon a time there was a nice, attractive farm. In the middle of the farm there was a maze. The maze was so huge that no one could ever find their way around it.

One day, some elephants came to disturb the farm. They were so big and noisy that the animals were all scared. The farmer was so worried. He didn't know how he was going to get the elephants out.

The farmer had a clever idea. He made the maze even more attractive by putting lots of delicious food at the end of it. The elephants were drawn to the maze and started to move in the right direction. They got so excited as they moved closer and closer to the tasty treats.

The farmer was very pleased as the elephants finally made it out of the maze and went on their way. He thanked them for taking the time to enjoy the maze and everyone in the farm was happy that their peaceful farm was no longer disturbed.

Now Jennifer couldn't wait to show her friends her beautiful spoon. She hugged it tightly and ran off with a smile on her face.
